title: Why Does Toast Land Butter-Side Down?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why does toast land butter-side down?
It's not bad luck, and it's not the weight of the butter.
Mostly, it's the height of your table.
As toast slides off the edge, it pivots on the rim and starts to spin.
But the spin is slow, and the fall is short: from a table, about four tenths of a second.
In that time, the toast only manages about half a turn.
It started butter up. Half a turn later: butter down.
From a table about three metres high, it would spin a full turn and land butter up.
So don't blame the butter. Blame the table.
